interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The postoperative pathology indicates a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2) and pathological stage pT3a. Favorable findings include negative surgical margins, absence of seminal vesicle invasion, and absence of lymphovascular invasion. The absence of documented nodal sampling means that the pNx status does not establish node-negative disease, which widens the uncertainty regarding regional spread. The preoperative PSA level is not documented. The primary prognostic factors are the T3a extension and the pNx nodal status. Countervailing findings are the negative surgical margins and the absence of seminal vesicle invasion. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are critical missing pieces of information that would revise the prognosis. Missing nodal sampling limits the ability to fully assess the extent of disease. The fixed estimated horizon is 43.46 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 26.08–60.84 months; its coverage has not been validated.
